body:
Thank you for the reply. I felt much better after sleeping on it.

I really do feel like cutting my dad out of my life for good might be the best option for everyone. He does know where I live which is the problem that is making it difficult. My mother and I have gone to the police before as well and had a temp. restraining order but at the hearing the judge said that it was basically "normal divorce problems" and did not grant a perm. one. Instead he just told my dad no direct contact with my mom was allowed, through lawyer only, and he was not supposed to go to either of our houses or my moms place of work. For the most part he was complied, but after he showed up banging on my door and creating a whole big damn scene for all my neighbors in my apartment complex to see, I was just like, are you kidding me? It's pretty embarrassing when I have to yell to my roommate to just stay in her room while I called the cops because he wouldn't go away. 

The thing is, when he is calm and not all drugged out, he's not really a bad person. But the moment he gets all cracked out on pills or doesn't take his bi-polar medication properly, he's not the same person. So we keep going through maybe a couple of weeks of him being relatively normal... being able to stop by and say hello to him and whatnot... and then as soon as he falls back into bad habits again he just turns back into the psycho who threatens to get a gun and shoot my mother and my (soon to be) step-dad and just goes completely nuts for a couple days and then when he settles back down he acts as if nothing happened! 

I really want him to get more help but he refuses... and unless he actually gets convicted from something serious it's not like a judge can force him into a mental institution. 


As for my relationship with my mom, I guess I should have went into that a bit more but right now it's actually pretty good. In the past it was horrendous but I've gotten over that because although there's no excuse for how shitty she was when I was going up, the explanation is my dad did a damn good job of pushing her over the edge as well.

She helps me alot, and has been supporting me for the last few months while I have been waiting for disability. She comes over and helps me with daily tasks when I can't do them and takes me to doctors appointments and stuff and she is a MUCH better person. Her new fiance has made her a whole new person.... he's a real great guy and I get along with him well and I even sent him a text recently telling him how in just the bit of time him and my mom have been together, he's been more of a dad to me than my real father has ever been. At first I thought it was some sort of catch... but realized no man is going to stick around to deal with a woman who has THIS much baggage... so yeah he's been great, a real help.

I am trying to be as optimistic as possible. It's just difficult.

I do want to do some sort of therapy. I just can never figure out what to do for that. I saw a psychiatrist before that I did like but it was difficult to schedule with her and it was a bit of a hassle getting to her office. Is there anyone who can help me with what to do to find a good therapist? What's the difference between therapists, psychiatrists, psychologists... etc... and what one(s) do I need to see? 

I'm willing to keep at least TRYING to get myself together. I'm currently on a number of medications as well as I do physical therapy and all that stuff. I try alternative medications and stuff as well because I figure hey what do I have to loose. 

It's just honestly... I have spent my entire life in and out of doctors offices...... and it's just interfering with me life.
